figures.caption: Table 2: Projected group-effect curve mT (w) = w⊤γ∗ for the Medicaid application, evaluated at percentiles of the pre-expansion uninsured rate Wg (the object plotted in Figure 2). The high-versus-low contrast uses the shared-donor covariance of Corollary 1; because it is a centered contrast, the intercept cancels.

Figure 2: Relationship between the group ATT τ̂g and the group covariate Wg (main application). Horizontal axis = pre-expansion (2008–2013) uninsured rate Wg, vertical axis = group ATT τ̂g. Each point has a 95% confidence interval (error bar) from donor leave-one-out jackknife, the solid line is the projection W⊤ g γ̂, and the light band is its pointwise 95% confidence band (Corollary 1), not simultaneous over the continuum. States with higher pre-expansion uninsured rates have larger reductions (R2 = 0.83, shared-donor SE (slope) 0.23), and states that are already low (MA, DC, VT) have smaller expected reductions (MA’s positive point estimate reflects the estimation instability near the floor). Wg can affect both the baseline level µgt(0) and the effect τg (Section 2.2), but the first-stage SDID removes the former and the second-stage projection extracts only the latter.

Table 1: Monte Carlo summary: what breaks under the naive treatment and what the proposed procedure repairs (representative designs; full tables in online Appendix H). The calibration trades size for power away from the null (e.g., at V = 0.145: naive 90% vs. calibrated 52%).

Figure 4: Event-time directed slope of the Clean Air Act application. Ĉ(e) = G−1 1 ∑ c(Wc − W̄ )τ̂c(e) is the projection of the county gap at post year e onto baseline PM2.5; bars are ±1.96 county-level standard errors. The directed reduction is weak in 2006, strengthens through 2008–2011, and attenuates by 2012, consistent with a lagged regulatory effect.

Figure 5: Application II (Clean Air Act). (A) County-wise SDID effects τ̂c sorted by baseline PM2.5. Error bars are ±1.96SE of the analytic noise based on the pre-treatment residuals, and the red dashed line is the mean −1.13µg/m3. County by county the noise is large, and the structure of heterogeneity is hard to read from the list of group-wise estimates. (B) Scatter of τ̂c against baseline PM2.5 (2000–2004 mean) and the directed projection. The solid line is the projection, and the band is the 95% band from the shared-donor kernel. Higher-baseline counties have larger reductions.

Figure 1: Rejection rates of the H0 : V = 0 test (nominal 5%, one-sided, B = 59). The bare TV (red ×) over-rejects at V = 0 with size 25–34%, whereas the placebo-calibrated T pc V (navy •) is controlled near the nominal 5% and its power rises as the heterogeneity V = Var(τg) increases (86% at V = 0.39).

Figure 3: Left: the two paths for V̂ (analytic = household-cluster survey variance; leave-out = household A/B) nearly agree. Right: the placebo null distribution of H0 : V = 0 and the observed V̂ (vertical line). Strongly rejected with T pc V = 24.7, rank p = 0.005.
